questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to chose a destination where everyone were speaking english in order to improve my english proficiency as well as being able to easily get around the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as all of the most important information were listed on the university's website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance is I had gotten all of the important information online before leaving Denmark.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different possibilities for campus housing but it were only available for 50-60% of exchange students which were picked at random.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I think a meal plan was available but i didn't use it and the apartment I ended up living in had a kitchen but it didn't came with any thing so all things for the kitchen needed to be purchased by yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They should know that it may be difficult to get it but it's quite fun to live in student housing if they get the chance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration progress were quite easy to look up the courses which to apply for and the process through mobility online. The registration at the host institution went smooth with the help from KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were help from KU and the people working through mobility online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3 of the 4 courses i most wanted and the last course I got was still on my top 10 which I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That it doesn't matter so much about which courses you choose before going there as it's possible to still change them once you get to the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3 of the courses were generally a bit easier compared to the once I am used to at KU while the last one was on the same level as I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching were very much the same just with some more quizzes to make every week and then midterms which are normally not a thing at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MICB: Immunology 302, PSYC: Principles of animal behavior 306, PSYC: Psychology of sport, SPAN: Beginner's spanish 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the courses I took as they were very interesting and I had some great teachers. Maybe keep in mind that the courses I took didn't necessarily have that much to do with my study at KU but were taken more as a little breather from my normal studies and to try something new.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The price for food were a little higher than what I had expected from home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really use any of them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different activities and a lot of clubs which made a lot of different things to choose from which also got a little overwhelming because of the amount. There were opportunities for everyone and I heard a lot of great things about them from others that tried them even though I didn't use them myself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to really use the nature in the area as it was an incredible experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go to the US and to go hiking or skiing depending on the season.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy as a lot of the canadian culture is like the one in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just jump into it as they are all really open and easy to speak to. Just keep in mind that many of them maybe are a couple of years younger than you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated that everyone is really open and a bit more welcoming than some danes are at first.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To bring a lot of different clothes as the weather is changing a bit and to be able to get into the nature. To really use the weekends and the breaks to go out and experience a lot of different things. To be prepared for Canada as being a country that is a bit more expensive compared to Denmark.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not on the spur of the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part were to be able to experience the incredible nature in the areas around campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the time difference from Vancouver to Denmark as it at times were a bit difficult to connect with friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
